title: Numbers from 0 to 10
topic: numbers in the feminine (for counting); phone numbers; age
why: The numbers from 0 to 10, in the form used for counting, let you give a phone number and say a child's age with בֶּן / בַּת. This is the foundation for numbers, which unit 6 will extend up to 100.

Counting from 0 to 10

Here are the numbers as you say them for counting, giving a phone number or an age.

NumberHebrewPronunciation
0אֶפֶסefes
1אַחַתakhat
2שְׁתַּיִםshtayim
3שָׁלוֹשׁshalosh
4אַרְבַּעarba
5חָמֵשׁkhamesh
6שֵׁשׁshesh
7שֶׁבַעsheva
8שְׁמוֹנֶהshmone
9תֵּשַׁעtesha
10עֶשֶׂרeser

The traps: four numbers start with sh (שָׁלוֹשׁ, שֵׁשׁ, שֶׁבַע, שְׁמוֹנֶה); עֶשֶׂר has a שׂ (dot on the left) that is read s; and שֵׁשׁ (6) and שֶׁבַע (7) come one after the other: don't mix them up.

Hebrew numbers also have a masculine form (אֶחָד, שְׁנַיִם…), used with masculine nouns. You'll see it later; for counting, you always use the form in this table, which is the feminine form.

", "

Your phone number

Israelis give their number digit by digit, in three groups. A cell phone number starts with אֶפֶס חָמֵשׁ (05):

אֶפֶס חָמֵשׁ שְׁתַּיִם, שָׁלוֹשׁ אַרְבַּע שֶׁבַע, אֶפֶס אַחַת תֵּשַׁע שְׁמוֹנֶה052-347-0198 [efes khamesh shtayim, shalosh arba sheva, efes akhat tesha shmone]

To ask for someone's number, learn this question as a whole; you'll understand its parts (הַ and שֶׁלְּךָ) later:

מָה הַמִּסְפָּר שֶׁלְּךָ? / מָה הַמִּסְפָּר שֶׁלָּךְ?What's your number? (to a man / to a woman) [ma ha-mispar shelkha? / ma ha-mispar shelakh?]

The word מִסְפָּר (mispar) means both \"number\" as in a phone number and \"number\" as in counting.

", "

How old are you?

In English, you \"are\" a certain age. In Hebrew, you're the \"son\" or \"daughter\" of a number of years: בֶּן (ben, son) for a boy or a man, בַּת (bat, daughter) for a girl or a woman. And כַּמָּה (kama) means \"how many / how much.\"

בֶּן כַּמָּה אַתָּה?How old are you? (to a boy) [ben kama ata?]
בַּת כַּמָּה אַתְּ?How old are you? (to a girl) [bat kama at?]
אֲנִי בֶּן שֶׁבַע. הִיא בַּת שָׁלוֹשׁ.I'm seven. She's three. [ani ben sheva. hi bat shalosh]

No word for \"years\" in the answer: the number is enough, just like \"I'm seven\" in English. For adults' ages you'll need the numbers up to 100 (unit 6); for now, talk about children: יֶלֶד (a boy) and יַלְדָּה (a girl).
